source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Judges 1–5 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 145 original source records are bound exactly once.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keep the opening after Joshua’s death and the question of which tribe leads the fighting.
verses.before: After the death of Joshua, the children of Israel asked the LORD, “Who will go up first for us against the Canaanites, to fight against them?”
verses.after: After Joshua died, the Israelites asked the LORD, “Who should go up first for us to fight the Canaanites?”
verses.tsw_comparator: After the death of Joshua, the children of Israel asked the LORD, “Who shall go up first for us against the Canaanites, to fight against them?”

verses.rationale: Retain Judah as the collective singular recipient of divine authorization and the hand image.
verses.before: The LORD said, “Judah will go up. Look, I have given the land into his hand.”
verses.after: The LORD answered, “Judah is to go up. I have given the land into his hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said, “Judah shall go up. Look, I have given the land into his hand.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the tribes as brothers and the reciprocal promise of military help.
verses.before: Then Judah said to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my allotted land, and let us fight against the Canaanites. Then I also will go with you into your allotted land.” So Simeon went with him.
verses.after: Judah said to his brother Simeon, “Come with me into my allotted territory, and we will fight the Canaanites. Then I will go with you into yours.” So Simeon went with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Judah said to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my allotted land, and let us fight against the Canaanites. Then I also will go with you into your allotted land.” So Simeon went with him.

verses.rationale: Keep both peoples, the location and exact number, with the shift to the group’s action.
verses.before: Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they struck down ten thousand of them at Bezek.
verses.after: Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hand. At Bezek they struck down ten thousand men.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they struck down ten thousand of them at Bezek.

verses.rationale: Retain the ruler’s name and repeated naming of both defeated peoples.
verses.before: They found Adoni-Bezek at Bezek and fought against him, and they struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
verses.after: They found Adoni-bezek at Bezek and fought him, defeating the Canaanites and Perizzites.
verses.tsw_comparator: They found Adoni-Bezek at Bezek and fought against him, and they struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

verses.rationale: Name the mutilation directly and preserve the sequence of pursuit, capture and injury.
verses.before: Adoni-Bezek fled, but they pursued him and seized him, and they cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
verses.after: Adoni-bezek fled, but they chased him down, captured him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Adoni-Bezek fled, but they pursued him and seized him, and they cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

verses.rationale: Keep seventy, the table image and mutilation, attributing the explanation of divine repayment to the speaker.
verses.before: Adoni-Bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off gathered scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me.” They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
verses.after: Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to gather scraps under my table. God has repaid me for what I did.” They brought him to Jerusalem, where he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Adoni-Bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off gathered scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me.” They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

verses.rationale: Retain the conquest claim here alongside the continued Jebusite residence later in the chapter.
verses.before: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They struck it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire.
verses.after: The people of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put it to the sword and set the city on fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They struck it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire.

verses.rationale: Keep all three regions and the descent notice.
verses.before: Afterward the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev, and the foothills.
verses.after: Afterward Judah’s people went down to fight the Canaanites living in the hill country, the Negev, and the lowlands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev, and the foothills.

verses.rationale: Preserve the alternate place name and all three named opponents.
verses.before: Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron—Hebron was formerly named Kiriath-Arba—and they struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
verses.after: Judah advanced against the Canaanites living in Hebron, formerly called Kiriath-arba. They struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron—Hebron was formerly named Kiriath-Arba—and they struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

verses.rationale: Keep Judah as the continuing collective agent without importing Caleb from the parallel account.
verses.before: From there they went against the inhabitants of Debir. The name of Debir was formerly Kiriath-Sepher.
verses.after: From there Judah advanced against the people of Debir, formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there they went against the inhabitants of Debir. The name of Debir was formerly Kiriath-Sepher.

verses.rationale: Preserve Caleb’s offer and both required actions, retaining clear wording shared with the source-parallel in Joshua.
verses.before: Caleb said, “Whoever strikes Kiriath-Sepher and captures it, I will give Achsah my daughter to him as wife.”
verses.after: Caleb said, “I will give my daughter Achsah in marriage to the man who attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Caleb said, “Whoever strikes Kiriath-Sepher and captures it, I will give Achsah my daughter to him as wife.”

verses.rationale: Keep the younger-brother relationship with its ambiguous attachment, explained in a note.
verses.before: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him Achsah his daughter as wife.
verses.after: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah in marriage.
verses.tsw_comparator: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him Achsah his daughter as wife.

verses.rationale: Make the implied Othniel explicit while preserving Achsah’s agency and the definite field in this version.
verses.before: When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What do you want?”
verses.after: When Achsah arrived, she urged Othniel to ask her father for the field. She got down from the donkey, and Caleb asked her, “What do you want?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What do you want?”

verses.rationale: Keep blessing as a tangible gift, both springs and Caleb’s explicit name as in this source.
verses.before: She said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water also.” So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
verses.after: “Give me a blessing,” she told him. “You have given me land in the Negev; give me springs of water too.” Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water also.” So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

verses.rationale: Preserve unnamed Kenite kinship, all locations and the unspecific people without harmonizing another account.
verses.before: The descendants of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up with the children of Judah from the City of Palms into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the Negev near Arad. They went and lived with the people.
verses.after: The descendants of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up from the City of Palms with Judah’s people into the wilderness of Judah, in the Negev near Arad. They went and settled among the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The descendants of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up with the children of Judah from the City of Palms into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the Negev near Arad. They went and lived with the people.

verses.rationale: Retain reciprocal help, the destruction and the resulting name linked to devotion.
verses.before: Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath and devoted it to destruction. The name of the city was called Hormah.
verses.after: Judah went with his brother Simeon. They struck the Canaanites living in Zephath and devoted the city to destruction. So it was named Hormah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath and devoted it to destruction. The name of the city was called Hormah.

verses.rationale: Keep all three capture claims and repeated territory without reconciling the next verse.
verses.before: Judah captured Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
verses.after: Judah captured Gaza and its territory, Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah captured Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.

verses.rationale: Make Judah the human agent while retaining the divine presence and the inability attributed to iron chariots.
verses.before: The LORD was with Judah, and Judah took possession of the hill country, but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plain because they had iron chariots.
verses.after: The LORD was with Judah, and Judah took possession of the hill country. But they could not drive out the people of the valley, because they had iron chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD was with Judah, and Judah took possession of the hill country, but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plain because they had iron chariots.

verses.rationale: Keep the gift’s authority, Caleb’s action and exact three.
verses.before: Hebron was given to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.
verses.after: Hebron was given to Caleb as Moses had promised, and he drove out the three sons of Anak from there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hebron was given to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.

verses.rationale: Retain Benjamin rather than substituting Judah from Joshua 15:63 and keep continued residence.
verses.before: But the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem. So the Jebusites have lived with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.after: But Benjamin’s people did not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. The Jebusites have lived with Benjamin’s people in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem. So the Jebusites have lived with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.

verses.rationale: Preserve Joseph’s collective household and divine presence before the second campaign.
verses.before: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
verses.after: Joseph’s household also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.

verses.rationale: Keep the scouting action and the town’s previous name.
verses.before: The house of Joseph sent men to spy out Bethel. The name of the city was formerly Luz.
verses.after: Joseph’s household sent scouts to Bethel, the town formerly called Luz.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house of Joseph sent men to spy out Bethel. The name of the city was formerly Luz.

verses.rationale: Retain the request and hesed pledge, linking the phrase to concrete protection as in Rahab’s story.
verses.before: The spies saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, “Please show us the entrance to the city, and we will show you steadfast love.”
verses.after: The scouts saw a man coming out of the town. “Please show us the way in,” they told him, “and we will show you loyal kindness.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The spies saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, “Please show us the entrance to the city, and we will show you steadfast love.”

verses.rationale: Keep the killing beside the explicit exception for the man’s entire kin group.
verses.before: He showed them the entrance to the city. They struck the city with the edge of the sword, but they let the man and all his family go.
verses.after: He showed them the way into the town, and they put the town to the sword. But they let the man and his whole clan go.
verses.tsw_comparator: He showed them the entrance to the city. They struck the city with the edge of the sword, but they let the man and all his family go.

verses.rationale: Preserve the new town rather than treating this as a return to Bethel.
verses.before: The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city, and he called its name Luz. That is its name to this day.
verses.after: The man went to the land of the Hittites, built a town, and named it Luz. That is its name to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city, and he called its name Luz. That is its name to this day.

verses.rationale: Retain all five places in this order, each dependent-town group and the Canaanites’ determination.
verses.before: Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-Shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, or the inhabitants of Ibleam and its villages, or the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages. The Canaanites persisted in living in that land.
verses.after: Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth-shean and its dependent towns, Taanach and its dependent towns, Dor and its dependent towns, Ibleam and its dependent towns, or Megiddo and its dependent towns. The Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-Shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, or the inhabitants of Ibleam and its villages, or the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages. The Canaanites persisted in living in that land.

verses.rationale: Keep the distinction between coercive labor and expulsion; do not present accommodation as equality.
verses.before: When Israel became strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but did not drive them out completely.
verses.after: When Israel grew strong, they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor, but they still did not drive them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Israel became strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but did not drive them out completely.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated location and absence of a forced-labor clause in this verse.
verses.before: Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived among them in Gezer.
verses.after: Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. The Canaanites remained among them in Gezer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived among them in Gezer.

verses.rationale: Keep both names as given here, residence and coerced labor.
verses.before: Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol. The Canaanites lived among them and became forced labor.
verses.after: Zebulun did not drive out the people of Kitron or Nahalol. The Canaanites remained among them and were subjected to forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol. The Canaanites lived among them and became forced labor.

verses.rationale: Preserve all seven entries without harmonizing names to Joshua’s list.
verses.before: Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco or the inhabitants of Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
verses.after: Asher did not drive out the people of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
verses.tsw_comparator: Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco or the inhabitants of Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.

verses.rationale: Retain the reversal: Israelites live among Canaanites, not the other way around.
verses.before: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.
verses.after: So Asher’s people lived among the Canaanites who inhabited the land, because they had not driven them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.

verses.rationale: Preserve the residence relationship and repeat both towns in the labor clause.
verses.before: Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-Shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-Anath, but lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land. Yet the inhabitants of Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath became forced labor for them.
verses.after: Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth-shemesh or Beth-anath. They lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, but subjected the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath to forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-Shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-Anath, but lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land. Yet the inhabitants of Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath became forced labor for them.

verses.rationale: Keep the Amorites as effective agents and Dan’s restricted movement.
verses.before: The Amorites pressed the children of Dan into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.
verses.after: The Amorites pressed Dan’s people back into the hill country and would not let them come down into the valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Amorites pressed the children of Dan into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.

verses.rationale: Preserve all places, the heavy-hand image and coerced labor.
verses.before: The Amorites persisted in living in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim, but the hand of the house of Joseph became heavy upon them, and they became forced labor.
verses.after: The Amorites were determined to remain at Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But Joseph’s household laid a heavy hand on them, and they were subjected to forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Amorites persisted in living in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim, but the hand of the house of Joseph became heavy upon them, and they became forced labor.

verses.rationale: Keep the Amorite label and both starting references, with Sela’s possible rock sense noted.
verses.before: The border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.
verses.after: The Amorite boundary ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.

verses.rationale: Keep the angel as speaker using divine first-person claims without supplying an identity explanation.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, “I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land that I swore to your ancestors. I said, ‘I will never break my covenant with you.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, “I brought you up from Egypt and into the land I swore to your ancestors to give you. I said, ‘I will never break my covenant with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, “I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land that I swore to your ancestors. I said, ‘I will never break my covenant with you.

verses.rationale: Retain both covenant prohibition and altar command, then the abrupt accusation.
verses.before: And you will make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you will tear down their altars.’ But you have not listened to my voice. What is this you have done?
verses.after: You must make no covenant with this land’s inhabitants; you must tear down their altars.’ But you have not obeyed my voice. What have you done?
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall tear down their altars.’ But you have not listened to my voice. What is this you have done?

verses.rationale: Preserve the sides image and snare while noting that thorns is supplied to complete the compressed Hebrew.
verses.before: So now I say: I will not drive them out before you, but they will become adversaries to you, and their gods will become a snare to you.”
verses.after: So now I say, ‘I will not drive them out before you. They will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will become a snare for you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: So now I say: I will not drive them out before you, but they will become adversaries to you, and their gods will become a snare to you.”

verses.rationale: Keep all Israel’s audible collective response.
verses.before: When the messenger of the LORD spoke these words to all the children of Israel, the people lifted up their voices and wept.
verses.after: When the angel of the LORD spoke these words to all the Israelites, the people raised their voices and wept.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the messenger of the LORD spoke these words to all the children of Israel, the people lifted up their voices and wept.

verses.rationale: Retain the place-name and worship response without inferring reform.
verses.before: They called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.
verses.after: They named that place Bochim and offered sacrifices to the LORD there.
verses.tsw_comparator: They called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Use retrospective tense to mark the return to Joshua’s lifetime after the opening death notice.
verses.before: When Joshua dismissed the people, the children of Israel went each to their inheritance to take possession of the land.
verses.after: Joshua had sent the people away, and the Israelites went each to their inheritance to take possession of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joshua dismissed the people, the children of Israel went each to their inheritance to take possession of the land.

verses.rationale: Preserve service, both generations and saw rather than knew in the parallel Joshua account.
verses.before: The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work that the LORD had done for Israel.
verses.after: The people served the LORD throughout Joshua’s lifetime and throughout the lifetimes of the elders who outlived him, who had seen all the great work the LORD had done for Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work that the LORD had done for Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the full identity, servant title and age in the repeated death notice.
verses.before: Joshua son of Nun, servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred ten years.
verses.after: Joshua son of Nun, the LORD’s servant, died at the age of one hundred ten.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua son of Nun, servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred ten years.

verses.rationale: Preserve the Heres form here rather than harmonizing Joshua’s Timnath-serah.
verses.before: They buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath-Heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
verses.after: They buried him within his inheritance at Timnath-heres, in Ephraim’s hill country, north of Mount Gaash.
verses.tsw_comparator: They buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath-Heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

verses.rationale: Keep the ancestral-gathering death image and both objects of the new generation’s lack of knowledge.
verses.before: And all that generation also was gathered to their ancestors. Another generation arose after them who did not know the LORD or the work that he had done for Israel.
verses.after: That whole generation was gathered to its ancestors. Another generation arose after them that did not know the LORD or the work he had done for Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all that generation also was gathered to their ancestors. Another generation arose after them who did not know the LORD or the work that he had done for Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the recurring evaluation and specific plural gods.
verses.before: The children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals.
verses.after: The Israelites did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes and served the Baals.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals.

verses.rationale: Retain departure from the rescuing God, surrounding peoples and concrete acts.
verses.before: They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt. They followed other gods from among the gods of the peoples around them, bowed down to them, and provoked the LORD to anger.
verses.after: They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of Egypt. They followed other gods, the gods of the peoples around them, and bowed down to them, provoking the LORD to anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt. They followed other gods from among the gods of the peoples around them, bowed down to them, and provoked the LORD to anger.

verses.rationale: Preserve this repeated abandonment and the distinct divine names.
verses.before: They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
verses.after: They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.

verses.rationale: Retain divine giving and selling, both hand images and Israel’s inability to stand.
verses.before: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of plunderers who plundered them. He sold them into the hand of their enemies around them, and they could no longer stand before their enemies.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel. He gave them into the hand of raiders who plundered them, and sold them into the hand of their enemies all around. They could no longer stand against their enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of plunderers who plundered them. He sold them into the hand of their enemies around them, and they could no longer stand before their enemies.

verses.rationale: Keep divine agency in harm, oath and the people’s suffering without specifying only military departures.
verses.before: Wherever they went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for harm, just as the LORD had spoken and just as the LORD had sworn to them. And they were in great distress.
verses.after: Whenever they went out, the LORD’s hand was against them to bring harm, just as he had said and sworn to them. They were in deep distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wherever they went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for harm, just as the LORD had spoken and just as the LORD had sworn to them. And they were in great distress.

verses.rationale: Retain the biblical title and concrete rescue role, with a selective explanation.
verses.before: Then the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hand of people who plundered them.
verses.after: Then the LORD raised up judges who rescued them from the hand of their raiders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hand of those who plundered them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the sexual infidelity metaphor and the contrast between generations.
verses.before: Yet they did not listen even to their judges, but prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly turned aside from the way in which their ancestors had walked, obeying the commandments of the LORD; they did not do so.
verses.after: Yet they would not listen even to their judges. They prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly left the path their ancestors had walked in obeying the LORD’s commandments; they did not do as their ancestors had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they did not listen even to their judges, but prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly turned aside from the way in which their ancestors had walked, obeying the commandments of the LORD; they did not do so.

verses.rationale: Keep the LORD as rescuer and the emotional response to groaning under real oppression.
verses.before: Whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge, for the LORD was moved by their groaning because of people who oppressed and crushed them.
verses.after: Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for them, he was with that judge and rescued them from their enemies’ hand throughout the judge’s lifetime. Their groaning under those who oppressed and crushed them moved the LORD to compassion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge, for the LORD was moved by their groaning because of those who oppressed and crushed them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated deterioration and all three acts of allegiance.
verses.before: But when the judge died, they turned back and acted more corruptly than their ancestors, following other gods, serving them, and bowing down to them. They did not cease from their practices or from their stubborn way.
verses.after: But when the judge died, they turned back and became more corrupt than their ancestors, following other gods, serving them, and bowing down to them. They would not give up their practices or their stubborn ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the judge died, they turned back and acted more corruptly than their ancestors, following other gods, serving them, and bowing down to them. They did not cease from their practices or from their stubborn way.

verses.rationale: Retain the covenant charge and divine speech continuing into its consequence.
verses.before: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he said, “Because this nation has transgressed my covenant that I commanded their ancestors and has not listened to my voice,
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he said, “Because this nation has violated the covenant I commanded their ancestors to keep and has not obeyed my voice,
verses.tsw_comparator: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he said, “Because this nation has transgressed my covenant that I commanded their ancestors and has not listened to my voice,

verses.rationale: Keep the exact remaining-nations frame without converting it into a new universal conquest claim.
verses.before: I also will no longer drive out before them any of the nations that Joshua left when he died,
verses.after: I too will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also will no longer drive out before them any of the nations that Joshua left when he died,

verses.rationale: Preserve the test and third-person LORD within divine speech, clarifying the purpose.
verses.before: in order to test Israel by them, whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors kept it, or not.”
verses.after: Through them I will test Israel, to see whether they will keep to the LORD’s way and walk in it as their ancestors did.”
verses.tsw_comparator: in order to test Israel by them, whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors kept it, or not.”

verses.rationale: Keep both negative statements and the timing rather than explaining away remaining peoples.
verses.before: So the LORD left those nations, not driving them out quickly, and he did not give them into the hand of Joshua.
verses.after: So the LORD left these nations in place. He did not drive them out quickly or give them into Joshua’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD left those nations, not driving them out quickly, and he did not give them into the hand of Joshua.

verses.rationale: Retain the test and the specified inexperienced group.
verses.before: These are the nations that the LORD left in order to test Israel by them—all in Israel who had not experienced any of the wars of Canaan—
verses.after: These are the nations the LORD left to test Israel—all those who had not known any of the wars in Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the nations that the LORD left in order to test Israel by them—all in Israel who had not experienced any of the wars of Canaan—

verses.rationale: Keep learning warfare as a stated purpose, alongside the obedience test in verse 4.
verses.before: only so that the generations of the children of Israel might know war, at least people who had not known it before:
verses.after: He did this so that later generations of Israelites would know warfare, teaching it to those who had not experienced it before.
verses.tsw_comparator: only so that the generations of the children of Israel might know war, at least those who had not known it before:

verses.rationale: Preserve every group, five rulers and the geographical span.
verses.before: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-Hermon to Lebo-Hamath.
verses.after: They were the five Philistine rulers, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the Lebanon mountains, from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
verses.tsw_comparator: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-Hermon to Lebo-Hamath.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated test and the Mosaic command relationship.
verses.before: They were for testing Israel, to know whether Israel would obey the commandments of the LORD that he had commanded their ancestors by the hand of Moses.
verses.after: They remained to test Israel, to learn whether Israel would obey the LORD’s commandments, which he had given their ancestors through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: They were for testing Israel, to know whether Israel would obey the commandments of the LORD that he had commanded their ancestors by the hand of Moses.

verses.rationale: Keep all six peoples and Israel’s position among them.
verses.before: So the children of Israel lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
verses.after: The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the children of Israel lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

verses.rationale: Make both directions of intermarriage and specific genders clear, preserving the service clause.
verses.before: They took their daughters for themselves as wives, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
verses.after: They took those peoples’ daughters as wives, gave their own daughters to those peoples’ sons, and served their gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took their daughters for themselves as wives, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.

verses.rationale: Keep the recurring evil formula, forgetting and Asheroth distinct from Ashtaroth.
verses.before: The children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
verses.after: The Israelites did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asheroth.

verses.rationale: Retain selling and serving under the named ruler, the region and eight years.
verses.before: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram-Naharaim. The children of Israel served Cushan-Rishathaim eight years.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim. The Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram-Naharaim. The children of Israel served Cushan-Rishathaim eight years.

verses.rationale: Preserve cry, divine provision and rescuing role, with the same kinship phrase as 1:13.
verses.before: Then the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for the children of Israel who saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
verses.after: The Israelites cried out to the LORD, and he raised up a rescuer who saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for the children of Israel who saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

verses.rationale: Keep Spirit, judging, war and repeated hand language; preserve the shorter regional name here.
verses.before: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-Rishathaim.
verses.after: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram, into his hand. His hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-Rishathaim.

verses.rationale: Retain the quiet/rest formula and exact period followed by death.
verses.before: Then the land had rest forty years. And Othniel son of Kenaz died.
verses.after: The land rested for forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the land had rest forty years. And Othniel son of Kenaz died.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated evaluation and the LORD’s strengthening of the oppressor.
verses.before: Again the children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: Again the Israelites did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes. The LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel because they had done what was evil in the LORD’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again the children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Make the implied ruler explicit and retain both allied groups and the collective capture.
verses.before: Eglon gathered to himself the children of Ammon and Amalek. He went and struck Israel, and they possessed the City of Palms.
verses.after: Eglon gathered the Ammonites and Amalek to him, went out, and struck Israel. They took possession of the City of Palms.
verses.tsw_comparator: Eglon gathered to himself the children of Ammon and Amalek. He went and struck Israel, and they possessed the City of Palms.

verses.rationale: Keep the named king, subjection and exact period.
verses.before: The children of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
verses.after: The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

verses.rationale: Keep left-handedness and tribal identity without assuming the precise cause of the right-hand restriction.
verses.before: Then the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up for them a deliverer, Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite, a man restricted in his right hand. The children of Israel sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.
verses.after: The Israelites cried out to the LORD, and he raised up a rescuer for them: Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The Israelites sent tribute with him to Eglon king of Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up for them a deliverer, Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite, a man restricted in his right hand. The children of Israel sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.

verses.rationale: Retain the rare source measure rather than inventing an exact modern length; preserve placement.
verses.before: Ehud made for himself a sword with two edges, a cubit in length, and strapped it under his clothing on his right thigh.
verses.after: Ehud made himself a double-edged sword, a gomed long, and strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ehud made for himself a sword with two edges, a cubit in length, and strapped it under his clothing on his right thigh.

verses.rationale: Keep the bodily description that matters to the ensuing action without ridicule added by the translator.
verses.before: He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
verses.after: He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon was a very fat man.
verses.tsw_comparator: He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.

verses.rationale: Keep the separation that enables the private return.
verses.before: When Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried the tribute.
verses.after: After presenting the tribute, Ehud sent away the people who had carried it.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried the tribute.

verses.rationale: Retain carved images with an alternative noted, identifying the king’s command and departure of attendants.
verses.before: But he himself turned back from the carved stones near Gilgal and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” The king said, “Silence!” And everyone who stood around him went out from him.
verses.after: But he himself turned back at the carved images near Gilgal. “I have a secret message for you, King,” he said. “Silence!” the king ordered, and all his attendants left him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he himself turned back from the carved stones near Gilgal and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” The king said, “Silence!” And all who stood around him went out from him.

verses.rationale: Make the two agents clear while preserving Ehud’s claim as speech.
verses.before: Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a word from God for you.” And he rose from his seat.
verses.after: Ehud approached Eglon as he sat alone in his cool upper room. “I have a message from God for you,” Ehud said. The king rose from his seat.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a word from God for you.” And he rose from his seat.

verses.rationale: Retain both sides of the body and direct killing action.
verses.before: Then Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into Eglon’s belly.
verses.after: Ehud reached with his left hand, drew the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into Eglon’s belly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into Eglon’s belly.

verses.rationale: Keep the physical sequence and a supported reading of the difficult final phrase, noting alternatives.
verses.before: The handle also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly, and the refuse came out.
verses.after: The hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over it. Ehud did not pull the sword out of his belly, and the excrement came out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The handle also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly, and the refuse came out.

verses.rationale: Retain the uncertain architectural term with a note, keeping escape and locking actions distinct.
verses.before: Then Ehud went out through the vestibule, closed the doors of the upper room behind him, and locked them.
verses.after: Ehud went out into the vestibule, closed the doors of the upper room behind him, and locked them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Ehud went out through the vestibule, closed the doors of the upper room behind him, and locked them.

verses.rationale: Render the covering-feet euphemism intelligibly while recording its literal image in a note.
verses.before: After he had gone out, Eglon’s servants came. They saw that the doors of the upper room were locked, and they said, “Surely he is covering his feet in the cool room.”
verses.after: After he left, the king’s servants came and found the upper-room doors locked. “He must be relieving himself in the cool room,” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: After he had gone out, Eglon’s servants came. They saw that the doors of the upper room were locked, and they said, “Surely he is covering his feet in the cool room.”

verses.rationale: Keep prolonged embarrassed delay, key and sudden discovery.
verses.before: They waited until they were embarrassed, but look, he did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened them, and look, their lord was fallen dead on the floor.
verses.after: They waited until they were embarrassed, but he still did not open the doors. So they took the key and opened them. There lay their lord on the floor, dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: They waited until they were embarrassed, but look, he did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened them, and look, their lord was fallen dead on the floor.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated landmark and named destination.
verses.before: Ehud escaped while they delayed. He passed beyond the carved stones and escaped to Seirah.
verses.after: Ehud escaped while they delayed. He passed the carved images and made his way to Seirah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ehud escaped while they delayed. He passed beyond the carved stones and escaped to Seirah.

verses.rationale: Keep arrival, signal and descent with Ehud at the front.
verses.before: When he arrived, he blew the ram’s horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill country, with him at their head.
verses.after: When he arrived, he blew the horn in Ephraim’s hill country. The Israelites came down from the hills with him leading them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he arrived, he blew the ram’s horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill country, with him at their head.

verses.rationale: Retain divine-gift claim, strategic crossings and absolute restriction.
verses.before: He said to them, “Follow me, for the LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand.” So they went down after him, seized the fords of the Jordan against Moab, and allowed no one to cross.
verses.after: “Follow me,” he told them, “for the LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand.” They followed him down, seized the Jordan crossings toward Moab, and let no one cross.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Follow me, for the LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand.” So they went down after him, seized the fords of the Jordan against Moab, and allowed no one to cross.

verses.rationale: Keep the approximate number, description and no-escape claim.
verses.before: They struck down about ten thousand Moabites at that time, all strong and able men, and not one escaped.
verses.after: At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all strong and capable men. Not one escaped.
verses.tsw_comparator: They struck down about ten thousand Moabites at that time, all strong and able men, and not one escaped.

verses.rationale: Preserve the hand image and exact rest period.
verses.before: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest eighty years.
verses.after: That day Moab was subdued under Israel’s hand, and the land rested for eighty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest eighty years.

verses.rationale: Keep the unusual weapon, six hundred and separate rescue notice without inventing a reign length.
verses.before: After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad, and he also saved Israel.
verses.after: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. He struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad; he too rescued Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad, and he also saved Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated evaluation and death transition without making Shamgar the stated predecessor.
verses.before: And the sons of Israel again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, after Ehud had died.
verses.after: After Ehud died, the Israelites again did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the sons of Israel again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, after Ehud had died.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine selling, the two men’s different roles and both locations.
verses.before: And the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth of the nations.
verses.after: The LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who ruled in Hazor. His army commander was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-haggoiim.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth of the nations.

verses.rationale: Keep the exact weapon count and oppression period, identifying the ruling power without removing harm.
verses.before: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he oppressed the sons of Israel harshly for twenty years.
verses.after: The Israelites cried out to the LORD. Jabin had nine hundred iron chariots and had cruelly oppressed them for twenty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he oppressed the sons of Israel harshly for twenty years.

verses.rationale: Keep Deborah’s sex, prophetic role, marriage designation and judicial agency; note the alternative sense of Lappidoth.
verses.before: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
verses.after: At that time Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.

verses.rationale: Retain the named tree, location and people seeking her decisions.
verses.before: She used to sit under the palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel came up to her for judgment.
verses.after: She would sit beneath Deborah’s Palm between Ramah and Bethel in Ephraim’s hill country, and the Israelites came up to her for judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: She used to sit under the palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel came up to her for judgment.

verses.rationale: Preserve Deborah’s question, divine command, both tribes and exact count.
verses.before: She sent and summoned Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali and said to him, “Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you? Go, gather your men at Mount Tabor, taking ten thousand from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun.
verses.after: She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali. “Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you?” she asked. “‘Go, draw your forces to Mount Tabor, and take ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: She sent and summoned Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali and said to him, “Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you? Go, gather your men at Mount Tabor, taking ten thousand from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun.

verses.rationale: Repeat draw for the matching human and divine actions; preserve military force and hand image.
verses.before: I will draw out Sisera, the commander of Jabin’s army, to meet you by the river Kishon with his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand.”
verses.after: I will draw Sisera, Jabin’s army commander, to you at the Wadi Kishon, along with his chariots and troops, and give him into your hand.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will draw out Sisera, the commander of Jabin’s army, to meet you by the river Kishon with his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand.”

verses.rationale: Keep the balanced repeated condition without supplying cowardice as a motive.
verses.before: Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.”
verses.after: Barak told her, “If you go with me, I will go. If you will not go with me, I will not go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.”

verses.rationale: Preserve her firm assent, loss of honor, selling and the specific woman without naming Jael prematurely.
verses.before: And she said, “I will surely go with you. Even so, the way you are going will not lead to your glory, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.” Then Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
verses.after: “I will certainly go with you,” she replied. “But the honor will not be yours on the journey you are taking, for the LORD will sell Sisera into a woman’s hand.” Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: And she said, “I will surely go with you. Nevertheless, the way you are going will not lead to your glory, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.” Then Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.

verses.rationale: Retain the count, the following-feet image and Deborah’s participation.
verses.before: Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up at his feet, and Deborah went up with him.
verses.after: Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh. Ten thousand men went up at his heels, and Deborah went with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up at his feet, and Deborah went up with him.

verses.rationale: Keep Hobab and the kinship designation as given, reading-tradition Zaanannim and the narrative aside.
verses.before: Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, from the sons of Hobab, father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak at Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.
verses.after: Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses’ father-in-law. He had pitched his tent by the oak at Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, from the sons of Hobab, father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak at Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.

verses.rationale: Retain the intelligence report and full identity.
verses.before: It was told to Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
verses.after: Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up Mount Tabor.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was told to Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated exact count and both endpoints.
verses.before: Sisera summoned all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth of the nations to the Wadi Kishon.
verses.after: Sisera summoned all his chariots—nine hundred iron chariots—and all the troops with him from Harosheth-haggoiim to the Wadi Kishon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sisera summoned all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth of the nations to the Wadi Kishon.

verses.rationale: Preserve Deborah’s commanding voice, question, divine agency and human descent.
verses.before: Deborah said to Barak, “Arise! For this is the day in which the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, with ten thousand men after him.
verses.after: Deborah told Barak, “Get up! This is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out ahead of you?” Barak went down Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deborah said to Barak, “Arise! For this is the day in which the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, with ten thousand men after him.

verses.rationale: Keep divine panic and sword warfare together, followed by the commander’s flight.
verses.before: And the LORD threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into confusion before Barak by the edge of the sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
verses.after: The LORD threw Sisera, all his chariots, and his whole army into panic before Barak’s sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into confusion before Barak by the edge of the sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.

verses.rationale: Preserve the pursuit endpoint and exhaustive killing claim.
verses.before: Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth of the nations, and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; not even one remained.
verses.after: Barak pursued the chariots and army as far as Harosheth-haggoiim. Sisera’s entire army fell by the sword; not one man remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth of the nations, and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; not even one remained.

verses.rationale: Keep Jael’s identity and the political relationship explaining Sisera’s refuge.
verses.before: Yet Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
verses.after: Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, Heber the Kenite’s wife. There was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and Heber’s household.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated invitation, reassurance and covering without assigning a motive.
verses.before: Jael went out to meet Sisera and said, “Turn aside, my lord, come in to me. Do not fear.” He entered her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
verses.after: Jael came out to meet Sisera. “Come in, my lord. Come in to me; do not be afraid,” she said. He entered her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jael went out to meet Sisera and said, “Turn aside, my lord, come in to me. Do not fear.” He entered her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.

verses.rationale: Preserve water requested versus milk given and repeated covering.
verses.before: He said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him.
verses.after: “Please give me a little water,” he said. “I am thirsty.” She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him.

verses.rationale: Keep the instruction to deny his presence as Sisera’s speech.
verses.before: He said to her, “Stand at the entrance of the tent. If someone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ then say, ‘No.’”
verses.after: He told her, “Stand at the tent entrance. If anyone comes and asks, ‘Is a man here?’ say, ‘No.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to her, “Stand at the entrance of the tent. If anyone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ then say, ‘No.’”

verses.rationale: Keep Jael as agent, the implements, the bodily wound, sleep and death without importing the song’s posture.
verses.before: Yet Jael wife of Heber took a tent peg and took the hammer in her hand. She went quietly to him and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground, while he was fast asleep and exhausted. And he died.
verses.after: But Jael, Heber’s wife, took a tent peg and a hammer in her hand. She approached him quietly and drove the peg through his temple into the ground. Exhausted, he had been fast asleep. He died.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jael wife of Heber took a tent peg and took the hammer in her hand. She went quietly to him and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground, while he was fast asleep and exhausted. And he died.

verses.rationale: Preserve the discovery through Jael’s invitation and the visible wound.
verses.before: And look, Barak was pursuing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man whom you seek.” He entered with her, and look, Sisera lay dead, with the peg in his temple.
verses.after: Barak came in pursuit of Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said, “Come, I will show you the man you are looking for.” He went in with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the peg in his temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, Barak was pursuing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man whom you seek.” He entered with her, and behold, Sisera lay dead, with the peg in his temple.

verses.rationale: Keep God as agent and Jabin as the separate royal opponent.
verses.before: So God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the sons of Israel on that day.
verses.after: That day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: So God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the sons of Israel on that day.

verses.rationale: Retain the increasingly heavy hand and final destruction without inventing a specific death scene.
verses.before: And the hand of the sons of Israel pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan until they cut off Jabin king of Canaan.
verses.after: The Israelites’ hand pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan until they cut him off completely.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the hand of the sons of Israel pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan until they cut off Jabin king of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Name both singers while opening the poem rather than turning it into prose summary.
verses.before: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang:
verses.after: That day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang:
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang:

verses.rationale: Choose a leadership reading for the difficult first phrase with loose-hair alternative noted; preserve parallel willing action and blessing.
verses.before: When leaders let their hair flow in Israel, when the people freely offer themselves, bless the LORD!
verses.after: When leaders took the lead in Israel, when the people freely offered themselves, bless the LORD!
verses.tsw_comparator: When leaders let their hair flow in Israel, when the people freely offer themselves, bless the LORD!

verses.rationale: Keep both audiences, emphatic repeated I and the two music verbs.
verses.before: Hear, O kings! Give ear, O rulers! I, to the LORD, I will sing; I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: Hear, kings! Listen, rulers! I will sing to the LORD—I will! I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, O kings! Give ear, O rulers! I, to the LORD, I will sing; I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain divine march and repeated dripping, keeping cosmic imagery and named places.
verses.before: O LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the fields of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens also poured, the clouds poured down water.
verses.after: LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the fields of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens dripped, the clouds dripped water.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the fields of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens also poured, the clouds poured down water.

verses.rationale: Keep the flowing/melting image and compressed this-Sinai expression instead of explaining a physical mechanism.
verses.before: The mountains quaked before the LORD, even Sinai before the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: Mountains flowed before the LORD, this Sinai before the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The mountains quaked before the LORD, even Sinai before the LORD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep both temporal figures and contrast between abandoned roads and indirect paths.
verses.before: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were abandoned, and travelers went by crooked paths.
verses.after: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the roads fell silent. Travelers took winding paths.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were abandoned, and travelers went by crooked paths.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated cessation and first-person mother identity, with the difficult village term noted.
verses.before: Village life ceased in Israel; it ceased until I, Deborah, arose, until I arose as a mother in Israel.
verses.after: Village life ceased in Israel; it ceased, until I arose, Deborah, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Village life ceased in Israel; it ceased until I, Deborah, arose, until I arose as a mother in Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep new gods, gates, rhetorical weapons question and forty thousand without resolving difficult syntax silently.
verses.before: They chose new gods; then war was in the gates. Was a shield seen, or a spear, among forty thousand in Israel?
verses.after: They chose new gods; then war came to the gates. Was a shield or spear to be seen among forty thousand in Israel?
verses.tsw_comparator: They chose new gods; then war was in the gates. Was a shield seen, or a spear, among forty thousand in Israel?

verses.rationale: Retain heart, commanders, willingness and the repeated blessing from verse 2.
verses.before: My heart is with the commanders of Israel, with people who freely offered themselves among the people. Bless the LORD!
verses.after: My heart is with Israel’s commanders, with those who freely offered themselves among the people. Bless the LORD!
verses.tsw_comparator: My heart is with the commanders of Israel, with those who freely offered themselves among the people. Bless the LORD!

verses.rationale: Preserve three social/travel positions and the invitation to recount, with uncertain cloth term noted.
verses.before: You who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on rich carpets, and you who walk on the road— tell of it!
verses.after: You who ride pale female donkeys, you who sit on saddlecloths, you who walk along the road—tell of it!
verses.tsw_comparator: You who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on rich carpets, and you who walk on the road— tell of it!

verses.rationale: Choose singers and villagers with explicit lexical uncertainty in notes, retain righteousness and repeated acts.
verses.before: At the sound of people who divide the flocks among the watering places, there they recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of his villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
verses.after: To the sound of singers at the watering places, there they recount the LORD’s righteous acts, his righteous acts for Israel’s villagers. Then the LORD’s people went down to the gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound of those who divide the flocks among the watering places, there they recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of his villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.

verses.rationale: Keep all four awaken calls and the gender-specific imperatives and captivity.
verses.before: Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, Barak! Lead away your captives, son of Abinoam!
verses.after: Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake! Sing a song! Rise, Barak! Lead your captives away, son of Abinoam!
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, Barak! Lead away your captives, son of Abinoam!

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult remnant/nobles relations and came-down repetition, with alternative syntax noted.
verses.before: Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down for me against the warriors.
verses.after: Then a remnant came down to the nobles; the LORD’s people came down to me among the warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down for me against the warriors.

verses.rationale: Keep the root image and all four tribal groups, retaining the ancient staff and role.
verses.before: From Ephraim came those whose root was in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples. From Machir commanders came down, and from Zebulun people who carry the staff of command.
verses.after: From Ephraim came those whose roots were in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your people. From Machir commanders came down, and from Zebulun those who carry the muster officer’s staff.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Ephraim came those whose root was in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples. From Machir commanders came down, and from Zebulun those who carry the staff of command.

verses.rationale: Retain my-leaders form, Issachar’s repeated name, passive sending, following-feet image and Reuben’s heart language; note compression.
verses.before: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was faithful to Barak; into the valley they rushed at his feet. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
verses.after: My leaders in Issachar were with Deborah; Issachar was with Barak, sent into the valley at his heels. Among Reuben’s divisions were great resolves of heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was faithful to Barak; into the valley they rushed at his feet. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.

verses.rationale: Keep the rebuke, sheepfold and piping images, and the changed heart noun beside the repeated phrase.
verses.before: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, listening to the piping for the flocks? Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
verses.after: Why did you stay between the sheepfolds, listening to the piping for the flocks? Among Reuben’s divisions were great searchings of heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, listening to the piping for the flocks? Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.

verses.rationale: Preserve the named absentees, geographical settings and question to Dan.
verses.before: Gilead remained beyond the Jordan. Dan—why did he stay with the ships? Asher sat at the seashore and remained by his landings.
verses.after: Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan. And Dan—why did he linger by the ships? Asher sat by the seashore and stayed beside his harbors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gilead remained beyond the Jordan. And Dan—why did he stay with the ships? Asher sat at the seashore and remained by his landings.

verses.rationale: Retain death-risk and the field heights, contrasting these groups with those who stayed. Consistency refinement: Add even to make the English degree expression intelligible while retaining the source’s life/death language and the parallel naming of Zebulun and Naphtali; preserve poetry.
verses.before: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives to death, and Naphtali also, on the heights of the field.
verses.after: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives even to death, and Naphtali too, on the heights of the field.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives to death, and Naphtali also, on the heights of the field.

consistency_history.prior_after: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives to death, and Naphtali too, on the heights of the field.
consistency_history.prior_rationale: Retain death-risk and the field heights, contrasting these groups with those who stayed.
consistency_history.rationale: Add even to make the English degree expression intelligible while retaining the source’s life/death language and the parallel naming of Zebulun and Naphtali; preserve poetry.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated battle, both place names and the denied silver gain.
verses.before: Kings came; they fought. Then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. They took no plunder of silver.
verses.after: Kings came; they fought. Then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by Megiddo’s waters. They took no plunder of silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: Kings came; they fought. Then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. They took no plunder of silver.

verses.rationale: Preserve the stars as fighting agents and the repeated verb without a meteorological explanation.
verses.before: From heaven the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.
verses.after: From heaven the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.
verses.tsw_comparator: From heaven the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.

verses.rationale: Keep three watercourse references and the self-address, with ancient/onslaught uncertainty noted.
verses.before: The torrent Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. March on, my soul, in strength!
verses.after: The Wadi Kishon swept them away, the ancient wadi, the Wadi Kishon. March on, my soul, with strength!
verses.tsw_comparator: The torrent Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. March on, my soul, in strength!

verses.rationale: Retain the sound and exact repeated galloping, identifying the strong ones in the horse context.
verses.before: Then the horses’ hooves hammered from the galloping, the galloping of his mighty steeds.
verses.after: Then the horses’ hooves pounded with the galloping, galloping of his mighty steeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the horses’ hooves hammered from the galloping, the galloping of his mighty steeds.

verses.rationale: Keep curse, repeated divine-help phrase and uncertain among/against warriors relation in a note.
verses.before: “Curse Meroz,” says the messenger of the LORD. “Bitterly curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD among the warriors.”
verses.after: “Curse Meroz,” said the angel of the LORD. “Curse its inhabitants bitterly, for they did not come to the LORD’s help, to the LORD’s help among the warriors.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Curse Meroz,” says the messenger of the LORD. “Bitterly curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD among the warriors.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the poem’s twofold blessing, specific woman and tent setting.
verses.before: Most blessed among women is Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite; most blessed among women in tents.
verses.after: Most blessed of women be Jael, Heber the Kenite’s wife; most blessed of women in tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: Most blessed among women is Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite; most blessed among women in tents.

verses.rationale: Keep the contrast of request and response and the vessel’s social image.
verses.before: He asked for water; she gave milk. In a noble bowl she brought curds.
verses.after: He asked for water; she gave milk. In a bowl fit for nobles she brought curds.
verses.tsw_comparator: He asked for water; she gave milk. In a noble bowl she brought curds.

verses.rationale: Keep both hands, implements and full violent verb sequence without replacing the poem with the prose account.
verses.before: She reached her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workers’ hammer. She struck Sisera; she crushed his head. She shattered and pierced his temple.
verses.after: Her hand reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workers’ hammer. She hammered Sisera, crushed his head, smashed and pierced his temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: She reached her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workers’ hammer. She struck Sisera; she crushed his head. She shattered and pierced his temple.

verses.rationale: Preserve the feet, repeated collapse verbs and final devastation in their given order.
verses.before: Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still. Between her feet he sank, he fell. Where he sank, there he fell—destroyed.
verses.after: Between her feet he sank, fell, lay still. Between her feet he sank and fell. Where he sank, there he fell—destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still. Between her feet he sank, he fell. Where he sank, there he fell—destroyed.

verses.rationale: Retain mother’s audible anxiety, window/lattice and both questions. Consistency refinement: Render the figurative footsteps of the chariots as clatter rather than assigning hooves to the vehicles. Retain both questions, the mother’s waiting, and poetic lines; explain the footsteps image in a selective note.
verses.before: Through the window she looked down, the mother of Sisera cried through the lattice: “Why is his chariot delayed in coming? Why are the hoofbeats of his chariots late?”
verses.after: Through the window Sisera’s mother looked, crying through the lattice: “Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why is the clatter of his chariots delayed?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Through the window she looked down, the mother of Sisera cried through the lattice: “Why is his chariot delayed in coming? Why are the hoofbeats of his chariots late?”

consistency_history.prior_after: Through the window Sisera’s mother looked, crying through the lattice: “Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why are the hoofbeats of his chariots delayed?”
consistency_history.prior_rationale: Retain mother’s audible anxiety, window/lattice and both questions.
consistency_history.rationale: Render the figurative footsteps of the chariots as clatter rather than assigning hooves to the vehicles. Retain both questions, the mother’s waiting, and poetic lines; explain the footsteps image in a selective note.

verses.rationale: Keep both the ladies’ reply and mother’s self-reassurance before the imagined plunder.
verses.before: The wisest of her noble women answer her, and she repeats their words to herself:
verses.after: Her wisest ladies answer her; she too repeats their words to herself:
verses.tsw_comparator: The wisest of her noble women answer her, and she repeats their words to herself:

verses.rationale: Retain the dehumanizing womb image for captive women, repeated plunder and textiles, and an explained reading of the difficult ending.
verses.before: “Are they not finding and dividing plunder? A woman, two women for each warrior; plunder of dyed cloth for Sisera, plunder of embroidered dyed cloth, two pieces of embroidered cloth for the neck of the plunderer?”
verses.after: “Surely they are finding and dividing plunder— a womb, two wombs for each man; plunder of dyed cloth for Sisera, plunder of dyed cloth, embroidered; dyed cloth, doubly embroidered, for the necks of those taking plunder.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Are they not finding and dividing plunder? A woman, two women for each warrior; plunder of dyed cloth for Sisera, plunder of embroidered dyed cloth, two pieces of embroidered cloth for the neck of the plunderer?”

verses.rationale: Preserve the prayer for enemies’ death, shift from your to him, sun image and separate narrator’s rest notice.
verses.before: So may all your enemies perish, O LORD! But may people who love you be like the sun when it rises in its strength. And the land had rest forty years.
verses.after: So may all your enemies perish, LORD! But may those who love him be like the sun when it rises in its strength. The land rested for forty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: So may all your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love you be like the sun when it rises in its strength. And the land had rest forty years.
